name: RUCAIBox/RecSysDatasets
what_it_holds: Curated download/preprocess toolkit (302 commits) converting many public recommender-system datasets into a unified 'atomic file' format for the RecBole library, including Foursquare (NYC and Tokyo check-ins) and Gowalla (global check-in dataset), plus 5 versions of the Yelp dataset (2018-2022), Amazon reviews (1996-2023), Tmall, and others.
why_useful: Fills gap #20 (party size / group travel / geotagged tourism datasets): Foursquare NYC/Tokyo and Gowalla give geotagged check-in mobility panels that are a free proxy for leisure travel/visitation patterns in specific cities, and the repo is a one-command way to pull and normalize them (rather than chasing the original academic hosts by hand).
license: unspecified on repo page (datasets carry their own academic-use terms)
geography: Foursquare: NYC, Tokyo; Gowalla: global; Yelp: US/Canada metros
time_coverage: Foursquare/Gowalla check-ins ~2009-2013 (historical, academic datasets); Yelp 2018-2022 dataset snapshots
size_hint: Foursquare NYC/Tokyo check-in sets are ~100k-500k rows each; Gowalla ~6.4M checkins over 196k users (as originally published)
themes: Restaurant and leisure proxies: OpenTable state of the industry CSV, Yelp dataset, Google Maps reviews scrapers, event ticket data
why_all: Fills gap #20 (party size / group travel / geotagged tourism datasets): Foursquare NYC/Tokyo and Gowalla give geotagged check-in mobility panels that are a free proxy for leisure travel/visitation patterns in specific cities, and the repo is a one-command way to pull and normalize them (rather than chasing the original academic hosts by hand).

name: Semantic Trails Dataset (semantic-trails)
what_it_holds: Source dataset behind Massive-STEPS: Foursquare-derived global-scale check-ins enriched with GeoNames/Wikidata geography and Schema.org venue-category mappings, in checkins.csv / venues.csv plus RDF/Turtle conversions; a public SPARQL endpoint (http://std.eurecom.fr/sparql) is also live. Actual CSV/TTL files are hosted on figshare, not committed to the repo. Apache-2.0 license; example records dated through Oct 2017.
why_useful: Larger, better-documented upstream source for the check-in data that Massive-STEPS subsets; worldwide coverage with population and category metadata could support a party-size / trip-type proxy or a cross-border destination-mix index (gap #20). Queryable via SPARQL without needing the full dump.
size_hint: not stated in README; feeds Massive-STEPS's 2.63M-checkin subset, so likely larger
themes: Twitter/X, Instagram, Flickr, TikTok tourism datasets: geotagged tourism flows, YFCC100M tourism subsets, Foursquare/Gowalla/Brightkite check-ins
why_all: Larger, better-documented upstream source for the check-in data that Massive-STEPS subsets; worldwide coverage with population and category metadata could support a party-size / trip-type proxy or a cross-border destination-mix index (gap #20). Queryable via SPARQL without needing the full dump.

name: scikit-mobility
what_it_holds: Python mobility-analysis toolkit (808 stars) with a bundled `data` module and `list_datasets()`/`load_dataset()` API; ships ready-to-load example datasets including `foursquare_nyc` (Foursquare check-ins of individuals moving in NYC) and `flow_foursquare_nyc` (derived flow/OD data), plus SF taxi and parking datasets and NYC spatial tessellation boundaries. Also supports loading arbitrary CDR/GPS/survey mobility data into standard TrajDataFrame/FlowDataFrame structures.
why_useful: Turns the NYC Foursquare check-in dataset (and any future check-in export) into an immediately usable flow/OD panel with a one-line loader -- useful as a acquisition method for building a tourism-flow or intra-city mobility proxy without hand-rolling parsing, and its FlowDataFrame generative models (gravity/radiation) could synthesize destination-choice baselines for comparison.
size_hint: n/a (tooling); foursquare_nyc dataset is the standard ~227k-checkin Yang et al. NYC subset
license: not confirmed (widely used academic-origin project, check repo LICENSE)
themes: Twitter/X, Instagram, Flickr, TikTok tourism datasets: geotagged tourism flows, YFCC100M tourism subsets, Foursquare/Gowalla/Brightkite check-ins
why_all: Turns the NYC Foursquare check-in dataset (and any future check-in export) into an immediately usable flow/OD panel with a one-line loader -- useful as a acquisition method for building a tourism-flow or intra-city mobility proxy without hand-rolling parsing, and its FlowDataFrame generative models (gravity/radiation) could synthesize destination-choice baselines for comparison.

name: Sequential-Recommendation-Datasets
what_it_holds: Download-and-preprocess scripts (228 stars, Apache-2.0, archived read-only as of May 2023) for 35+ sequential-recommendation datasets, including Foursquare NYC and Tokyo check-ins and Gowalla, alongside Amazon/Yelp/MovieLens etc. Provides user- or time-based splitting and PyTorch DataLoader wrappers; does not host raw data itself, only pull/parse code.
why_useful: One-command pull-and-clean pipeline for the two classic location check-in datasets (Foursquare NYC/Tokyo, Gowalla) that other tourism-mobility repos (HGARN, scikit-mobility) reference informally -- useful as tooling to reconstruct those panels for a party-size or destination-choice cut.
themes: Twitter/X, Instagram, Flickr, TikTok tourism datasets: geotagged tourism flows, YFCC100M tourism subsets, Foursquare/Gowalla/Brightkite check-ins
wildcard: a computational social scientist who works with Reddit dumps
why_all: One-command pull-and-clean pipeline for the two classic location check-in datasets (Foursquare NYC/Tokyo, Gowalla) that other tourism-mobility repos (HGARN, scikit-mobility) reference informally -- useful as tooling to reconstruct those panels for a party-size or destination-choice cut.

Gowalla/Foursquare geotagged check-ins are the closest free analogue to Twitter tourism-flow / cross-border travel-pattern datasets named in gap #20 (party size / group travel / cross-border share proxies) -- dated (2009-2011) but a genuine geotagged human-mobility panel with venue-category labels (some travel/hospitality-related) that could validate a tourist-flow methodology before applying it to newer data.

name: COVID19USFlows-WeeklyFlows (GeoDS Lab, UW-Madison)
what_it_holds: Weekly-aggregated companion to COVID19USFlows: SafeGraph-derived origin-destination visitor/population flow CSVs at census-tract, county, and state scale, Jan 2019 through 2021. MIT licensed.
why_useful: Weekly cadence is a better match to the pitch's mixed-frequency nowcasting cadence than the daily version and is smaller to work with; same value case as the daily-flows repo above (SafeGraph mobility as a demand-shock and elasticity calibration input, gap #5/#11/#17).
size_hint: Multiple CSV files, weekly cadence, split by geography and repo size limits
last_activity: part of the same actively-cited GeoDS Lab research initiative
themes: Public-health and mobility indices: Google/Apple mobility archives, Cuebiq, SafeGraph/Advan/Dewey samples, Placer.ai-like foot traffic, mobility datasets by city
why_all: Weekly cadence is a better match to the pitch's mixed-frequency nowcasting cadence than the daily version and is smaller to work with; same value case as the daily-flows repo above (SafeGraph mobility as a demand-shock and elasticity calibration input, gap #5/#11/#17).
